boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's gx_bgcnt.c, 0x02054d38..0x020551f0: for each of BG0..BG3 the screen-base and character-base getter of the main engine (G2_) and the sub engine (G2S_), sixteen functions with no gaps. Each matches by body the function in the same position in pret's pokediamond GX_bgcnt.c (16 of 16).

Order: pret's file defines the getters BG0 screen through BG3 character, each G2S_ getter directly after its G2_ twin. mwccarm emits the bodies in reverse, so G2S_GetBG3CharPtr is lowest at 0x02054d38 and G2_GetBG0ScrPtr highest at 0x020551bc.

Vram__Map (0x02054c80..0x02054d38) below is the last of arm9/GX_VramCnt; G2x_ChangeBlendBrightness_ (0x020551f0) above is the first of arm9/G2x (gx_g2.c). Neither calls into or is called by the getter set.
No data, bss or RTTI: the getters read fixed I/O registers and return computed addresses, so nothing but the sixteen functions emits.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows arm9/G2x.

Written in C, as the SDK is, under the SDK's own names (G2_GetBG0ScrPtr ...). It was src/engine/gx/G2.cpp, whose coined C++ namespaces G2 and G2S mangled thirteen of the names and left the main engine's BG0, BG1 and BG3 character getters at their addresses (func_02054efc, func_02054ea8, func_02054d88). The rename changes no code.
The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order; the emitted object carries the sixteen functions ascending 0x02054d38..0x020551f0.
